Estimate a time-varying PSF matrix from an alkane ladder TIC

Source: R/estimate_psf_from_std.R
estimate_psf_from_std.Rd

Estimates the time-varying chromatographic point-spread function (PSF) from the total ion chromatogram of an alkane ladder standard and returns a sparse convolution design matrix. The baseline is estimated as a low-degree B-spline quantile regression underapproximation. Major ladder peaks are detected in the baseline-corrected TIC, each local peak profile is smoothed as a non-negative, centroid-centred, log-concave unit-sum PSF, and the local log-PSFs are interpolated or extrapolated over retention time. The default support is inferred from the complete local peak windows and the output scan spacing, allowing broad and narrow peaks to share a suitable grid without imposing a fixed number of support points.

The returned sparse matrix X has one column per requested output retention time. Column j contains the PSF centred at output_timepoints[j] and is normalised to sum to one. It can be passed as the X argument to L0glm_sparse_deco for deconvolution with a time-varying PSF.

Usage

estimate_psf_from_std(
  y,
  family = stats::poisson(link = "identity"),
  baseline_df = 10L,
  output_timepoints = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  baseline_tau = 0.05,
  n_peaks = NULL,
  peak_min_distance = NULL,
  peak_height = NULL,
  peak_snr = 5,
  support_fraction = 0.005,
  psf_mass = 0.999,
  support_quantile = 0.95,
  kernel_half_width = NULL,
  psf_length = NULL,
  psf_nknots = NULL,
  psf_tau = 0.75,
  psf_weight_power = 0.5,
  log_floor = 1e-12,
  drop_tol = 1e-10,
  return_details = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

y

Numeric vector containing the alkane ladder total ion chromatogram. If time is omitted and names(y) are numeric, the names are used as retention times.

family

GLM family object with an identity link, or one of "poisson", "gaussian" or "gamma". The family is used to validate the intended non-negative identity-link noise model and to set family-aware weights for log-concave local PSF smoothing.

baseline_df

Integer; degrees of freedom / number of spline knots for the low-dimensional B-spline baseline underapproximation.

output_timepoints

Numeric vector of retention times for the rows and columns of the returned PSF matrix. Defaults to the input time.

time

Optional numeric vector of retention times for y.

baseline_tau

Quantile used for the B-spline baseline underapproximation. Small values such as 0.02 to 0.10 are useful for chromatograms with positive peaks.

n_peaks

Optional integer number of major ladder peaks to keep. For a C9–C40 ladder this is typically 32. If omitted, all sufficiently prominent local maxima after non-maximum suppression are used.

peak_min_distance

Optional minimum distance, in retention-time units, between selected peaks. If omitted, a conservative value is inferred from the chromatogram range.

peak_height

Optional minimum baseline-corrected peak height. If omitted, a robust threshold is inferred from the baseline residuals.

peak_snr

Signal-to-noise multiplier used when peak_height is inferred automatically.

support_fraction

Fraction of the peak apex height used to trim local peak windows. The trimming is also bounded by neighbouring selected peaks.

psf_mass

Fraction of each local peak's baseline-corrected signal mass used to infer the automatic PSF support. The default uses the central 99.9 percent of each detected peak and avoids very long low-intensity tails dominating kernel_half_width.

support_quantile

Quantile of detected local peak half-widths used to infer kernel_half_width when it is not supplied. Larger values keep more tail support but make the returned sparse matrix less sparse.

kernel_half_width

Optional PSF half-width in retention-time units. If omitted, it is estimated from the detected peak windows.

psf_length

Optional odd integer number of support points used for the local PSF grid. If omitted, it is inferred from kernel_half_width and the median spacing of output_timepoints.

psf_nknots

Optional number of knots for the log-concave local PSF smoothing. If omitted, a small value is inferred from psf_length.

psf_tau

Quantile used by the constrained log-spline smoother for each local PSF. Values above 0.5 fit a more upper-envelope-like log-concave curve and tend to preserve heavier tails.

psf_weight_power

Exponent applied to the local normalised peak profile when constructing log-spline weights. Poisson-like weighting corresponds to 1; the default 0.5 downweights tails less and usually gives more realistic early alkane peak tails. Use 0 for equal weights.

log_floor

Positive relative floor used before interpolating local PSFs on the log scale.

drop_tol

Relative tolerance for dropping tiny PSF entries from the sparse matrix.

return_details

Logical; if TRUE, return a list with X and diagnostic details. If FALSE, return X directly with the same diagnostics attached as attributes.

verbose

Logical; print a short summary of the fitted baseline, peak detection, and PSF support.

Value

By default, a sparse dgCMatrix with dimensions length(output_timepoints) x length(output_timepoints). With return_details = TRUE, a list with components X, baseline, residual, peak_indices, peak_timepoints, peak_heights, psf_offsets, psf_kernels, and family.

See also

L0glm_sparse_deco, log_conc_smooth, convmatrix

Examples

data(GCMS_data1)
# total ion chromatogram of C9 to C40 alkane ladder
tic <- attr(GCMS_data1, "alkanes_TIC")

plot(x=as.numeric(names(attr(GCMS_data1, "alkanes_TIC"))),  
           y=attr(GCMS_data1, "alkanes_TIC"), 
           xlab="Retention time (min)", 
           ylab="Total ion intensity", 
           main="C9 to C40 alkane ladder standard", 
           col = "blue",
           type="l")

# Estimate the time-varying PSF with automatic support and scan-grid length.
fit <- estimate_psf_from_std(
  y = tic,
  family = poisson(identity),
  baseline_df = 10,
  output_timepoints = as.numeric(names(tic)),
  n_peaks = 32,
  return_details = TRUE
)

# fitted peaks:
matplot(fit$psf_offsets, t(fit$psf_kernels[1:32, ]),
        type = "l", lty = 1,
        xlab = "Offset from centroid (min)",
        ylab = "PSF density",
        main = "Fitted peak shapes")

# estimated time-varying PSF:
matplot(fit$X[seq(1, nrow(fit$X), by = 1), seq(1, ncol(fit$X), by = 300)], 
        type = "l", col = "blue", lty = 1,
        xlab = "Time index", ylab = "Intensity",
        main = "Estimated time-varying PSF")

# deconvolute GC/MS chromatogram using estimated time-varying PSF:
X <- estimate_psf_from_std(
  y = tic,
  family = poisson(identity),
  baseline_df = 10,
  output_timepoints = as.numeric(rownames(GCMS_data1)),
  n_peaks = 32,
  return_details = FALSE
)
matplot(X, 
        type = "l", col = "blue", lty = 1,
        xlab = "Time index", ylab = "Intensity",
        main = "Estimated time-varying PSF\nfor chromatogram subsection")
system.time(fit.mc <- L0nnpois(
  X,
  GCMS_data1,
  lambda = "gic",
  grouped = TRUE,
  relaxed = TRUE,
  parallelize = TRUE,
  ncores = round(parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE))
))

plotmat(GCMS_data1, 
        xlab = "Elution time (min)",
        ylab = "Mass (m/z)",
        main = "Section of Cataglyphis iberica\nant queen cuticular GC/MS profile")
sum(Matrix::rowSums(fit.mc$coefficients)!=0)
rows = Matrix::rowSums(fit.mc$coefficients)[which(Matrix::rowSums(fit.mc$coefficients)!=0)]
nrows = rows/max(rows)
abline(v = which(Matrix::rowSums(fit.mc$coefficients)!=0),
       col = sapply(nrows, function (alpha) adjustcolor("cyan", alpha = alpha)))
# TODO: cluster together compounds with similar mass spectra when joined elution profiles
# are log concave

hist(Matrix::rowSums(fit.mc$coefficients)[which(Matrix::rowSums(fit.mc$coefficients)!=0)])

for (i in 1:length(which(Matrix::rowSums(fit.mc$coefficients)!=0)) ) {
  plot(x = as.numeric(colnames(GCMS_data1)),
       y = fit.mc$coefficients[which(Matrix::rowSums(fit.mc$coefficients)!=0)[i],],
       main = paste0("Spectrum deconvoluted compound ", as.character(i),
                     "\nRT ", rownames(GCMS_data1)[which(Matrix::rowSums(fit.mc$coefficients)!=0)[1]], " min"),
       ylab = "Intensity", xlab = "Mass",
       col = "blue", type = "h")
}
